title: Version negotiation advertises v2 and v1, which can't be spoken
description: UdxVersion.supportedVersions is [3, 2, 1] and is sent in VERSION_NEGOTIATION, but packets of any version other than 3 are dropped (v3 changed the STREAM frame layout). Advertise only v3, as js-udx does.

title: Streams opened by go-udx/js-udx collide: registered under local id 0
description: Found while fixing STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED routing. go-udx and js-udx never learn the peer's stream id for a stream they open, so they address it to destination 0. createIncoming (socket.dart _processPacketFrames) uses the packet's destination id as the new stream's LOCAL id, so every stream they open is registered as stream 0. The first works by accident; a second concurrent one is looked up as _registeredStreams[0] first and its data lands in the FIRST stream. Fix: allocate our own local id for incoming streams (as go-udx does: odd for initiator, even for responder) and record the sender's id as remoteId. go-udx's multistream interop tests don't catch it: Dart opens all the streams there. Single-stream use (libp2p upgrades over one stream) is unaffected.

title: Go interop test and interop servers still assert/stamp version 2
description: test/interop/go_udx_interop_test.dart asserts the echoed version is 0x2, and both bin/interop_server.dart and go-udx's cmd/interop-server stamp Version=V2 on replies, though the frames are v3. A v3 multiplexer drops those replies. Update both servers and the assertion to v3.

title: ACKs carry no SACK history, so peers recover every loss by RTO
description: Found while fixing ACK range encoding. _sendConnectionAck sends an ACK for each ack-eliciting packet and then clears _receivedPacketSequences, so each ACK names about one sequence and never carries gap ranges. go-udx and js-udx detect loss from SACK gaps (3-packet / 9/8-RTT thresholds); with no ranges they fall back to the RTO (>=200 ms) for every lost packet sent to a Dart receiver. Fix: keep a sliding window of received sequences (go-udx's recvTracker: 512-sequence bitmap, at most 5 ranges) and adopt go-udx's ACK policy (every 2nd packet, immediately on gap/SYN/FIN, else SRTT/4 clamped to 1-25 ms).

title: Anti-amplification validates on the 2nd packet, which proves nothing
description: UDPSocket marks a server-side peer address validated once >= 1000 bytes arrive or the handshake completes, which happens on the first packet; a spoofer can do both. RFC 9000 §8.1 validation needs proof the peer received something we sent. js-udx sends a PATH_CHALLENGE in the acceptor's first packet and validates on the matching PATH_RESPONSE (go-udx and dart-udx both answer), retrying a few times.

title: Skipped test files reference removed test hooks
description: ack_handling_test.dart and loss_detection_test.dart are @Skip'ped wholesale (per-stream PM/CC moved to socket level) and no longer compile (congestionControllerForTest, packetManagerForTest, getSentPacketsTestHook). dart analyze reports errors for them. Rewrite against socket-level sequencing or delete.

title: ACK frame length counts ECN fields that are never encoded or decoded
description: AckFrame.length adds a flag byte and 8 bytes per ECN count when ect0Count/ect1Count/ceCount are set, but toBytes never writes them and fromBytes never reads them, so a frame with ECN counts encodes shorter than its declared length (trailing zero bytes that a peer parses as PADDING, or worse). Either implement ECN in the wire format in step with go-udx, or remove the fields.

title: Stateless reset tokens are never exchanged
description: sendStatelessReset and registerResetToken exist, but nothing sends or learns tokens, so stateless reset never works. js-udx sends its token in a NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame (seq 0, cid = its local CID) when a secret is configured, registers tokens from received NEW_CONNECTION_ID frames, and resets packets for CIDs left unclaimed for 3 s. With the frame numbering fixed (0x10), dart-udx can now parse those frames.

title: PMTUD never raises the MTU: probes are never acknowledged
description: buildProbePacket sends an MTU_PROBE frame only, and this side acknowledges only packets containing STREAM or PING frames, so every probe 'times out' after 3 s and the search settles at 1280. Fix: put a PING in each probe (js-udx sends PING + MTU_PROBE under a fresh nonzero sequence). Also: currentMtu isn't used to size STREAM payloads (fixed 1384), so discovery has no effect even when it works.
